name: Devil's-bit scabious
family: Caprifoliaceae, the honeysuckle family (the scabious group, once its own family, Dipsacaceae, the teasel family)
grown_as: A native perennial wild flower of damp meadows, by William's pond. The food plant of the marsh fritillary butterfly.
habit: A clump-forming perennial with a basal rosette and slender, sparingly branched stems 30 to 80 cm (up to 1 m). The short rootstock ends abruptly, as if bitten off.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the base; a few opposite pairs up the stem
leaf.outline: Basal leaves oblong to elliptic or spoon-shaped, 5 to 25 cm; stem leaves narrow lance-shaped and small
leaf.margin: Smooth, or a few distant shallow teeth on the stem leaves
leaf.veins: A strong pale midrib; side veins faint
leaf.surface: Thinly hairy or nearly smooth, slightly firm
leaf.stalk: Basal leaves on a short winged stalk; stem leaves stalkless
leaf.colour: Dark green, often blotched or edged purple

flower.form: A small round dome (half a ball) of florets all about the same size, with no larger outer ring
flower.petals: Each floret a small tube with four lobes
flower.colour: Blue-violet to mauve-purple, now and then pink or white
flower.centre: None: the whole dome is florets. Long stamens with dark purple anthers stick out, giving a fuzzy look
flower.behind: Two or three rows of green, hairy bracts under the head
flower.carried: At the tips of long, slender stems, often in threes (one at the top and one on each of a pair of side branches), upright

fruit: A small round brown seed head. Each seed is tiny and hairy, in a four-angled collar with five short bristles at the top.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves. The first true leaves are oval, undivided and stalked.
winter: A flat rosette of dark green oblong leaves, often reddish-purple, stays at the soil.

leaf: undivided oblong to spoon-shaped basal leaf
bloom: round domed head with all florets the same size, no frilly outer ring
long stamens with dark anthers making it fuzzy
seed: tiny seed in a four-angled collar with short bristles
young: flat rosette of oblong dark green leaves
flower: slender tall stems, branching in pairs, each with a round blue-violet head
few small narrow stem leaves in opposite pairs
seedhead: small round brown seed heads on bare stems
dormant: flat rosette of oblong dark green leaves, often purple-tinged

look_alikes: Field scabious (Knautia arvensis) has lobed leaves, bristly stems and flatter heads with larger outer florets. Small scabious has finely cut leaves and a frilly outer ring. Sheep's-bit (Jasione) is in the bellflower family, with alternate leaves and flatter heads of tiny star-shaped flowers. Round-headed rampion has alternate leaves and claw-like flowers.
